desc:
The number of set bits of a non-negative integer is the number of 1 digits in its binary representation. For example, 7 = 111 has three set bits and 8 = 1000 has one.

Return the array nums sorted by number of set bits in ascending order. Numbers with the same number of set bits are ordered by value, smaller first.

Example: nums = [7, 8, 3, 1] has set-bit counts 3, 1, 2, 1, so the answer is [1, 8, 3, 7].
hints: Every number has a sort key that is not the number itself. What is it?
Count the set bits of x with a loop: add x & 1, then shift x right by one, until x is zero.
Sort with the pair (bit count, value) as the key, so equal bit counts fall back to the value.
editorial: The order is defined by two keys: first the population count, then the value itself. Compute the population count of each number by repeatedly adding the lowest bit and shifting (at most 30 steps for values up to 109), or by Kernighan's trick x &= x - 1 which runs once per set bit.

Sort by the tuple (count, value). Since tuples compare element by element, the value only matters when the counts are equal. Sorting costs O(n log n) and computing all keys O(n log V) for the largest value V.
